name: Zinger Burger
description: Crispy spicy chicken zinger-style burger with evenly cooked chicken fillets, a craggy seasoned coating, lettuce and creamy mayonnaise in toasted buns.
ingredients: ½ cup milk or water for egg wash
1 tsp salt, divided or to taste
method: Pat the chicken fillets dry and flatten thicker areas so each piece has a fairly even thickness. Season with some of the salt, chilli, paprika and black pepper, then refrigerate briefly while preparing the coating.
Combine the flour and cornflour with the remaining seasoning in a wide bowl. In a second bowl, beat the egg with the milk or water until uniform.

Dip each fillet into the egg mixture, let excess drip off, then press firmly into the seasoned flour. Pinch some flour onto the surface to create irregular craggy pieces that become crisp during frying.
Heat the frying oil over medium heat and cook the fillets in manageable batches. Avoid overcrowding, which lowers the oil temperature and can make the coating greasy.
Turn as needed and continue frying until the coating is deeply golden and the chicken is fully cooked through. Check the thickest part rather than relying only on crust colour.
Drain on a rack or absorbent paper while lightly toasting the cut sides of the buns. Assemble with mayonnaise, lettuce and the hot chicken fillet and serve immediately.
tips: Flatten fillets to an even thickness so the centre cooks before the coating becomes too dark.
If the coating browns very quickly, lower the oil temperature rather than serving chicken that may still be raw inside.
storage: The burger is best assembled fresh. Cool leftover cooked chicken promptly, refrigerate covered and reheat thoroughly before putting it into a freshly assembled bun.
image_alt: Crispy chicken zinger-style burger with craggy seasoned coating, lettuce and mayonnaise
image_caption: Evenly flattened chicken fillets coated in seasoned flour, fried crisp and assembled in toasted buns.
technique: Even chicken thickness is the safety and texture key. Build a craggy coating by pressing flour onto the egg-washed fillet, then fry at steady medium heat so the centre cooks before the crust becomes too dark.
doneness_cues: Fillets should be similar thickness after flattening.
Coating should look rough and well adhered before frying.
Oil should bubble steadily rather than smoke.
Thickest chicken area must be fully cooked while the crust stays crisp.
mistakes: Crowding the pan and dropping oil temperature.
Using very hot oil that browns the crust before the centre cooks.
Assembling too early and steaming the crisp coating inside the bun.
substitutions: Use boneless thigh for a juicier burger with adjusted shape.
Milk or water both work in the egg wash.
Add chilli gradually to the flour instead of relying on hot sauce to mask bland chicken.
reheating: Reheat cooked fillets with dry heat until hot and crisp, then assemble fresh.
serving: Toast buns lightly and assemble only when the chicken is ready to serve.
